nodes.statement: The unit flow submits a second bdev reset while the first controller reset is still active.
The controller-reset function reports EBUSY for the concurrent reset request.
The bdev reset request enters bdev_nvme_reset and is dispatched toward controller reset handling.
The reset path sends work to the app-thread reset handler before invoking the controller reset.
The app-thread handler acquires the controller and bdev I/O context needed to manage the reset.
The controller's pending_resets queue retains ownership of the concurrent bdev I/O until reset completion.
An EBUSY controller reset appends the concurrent bdev I/O to pending_resets and returns.
Controller reset completion drains every bdev I/O from pending_resets.
Each drained pending reset receives success or failure derived from the controller-reset result.
The completion loop removes each queued request and resumes its bdev I/O completion path.
Reset completion unfreezes the relevant I/O paths and completes the retained reset request resources.
test_pending_reset observes both reset I/Os succeed normally and both fail after controller removal.
The test_pending_reset unit test is the source-backed oracle for concurrent reset queuing and completion.

edges.statement: Submitting the second reset while the first is active causes the controller reset path to return EBUSY.
The bounded concurrent reset request reaches bdev_nvme_reset with the first reset still active.
bdev_nvme_reset dispatches the request through the app-thread reset call chain.
The app-thread handler resolves the controller context before attempting controller reset.
When the controller is busy, its pending queue retains the acquired bdev I/O context.
The controller-owned queue is mutated by appending the concurrent reset request.
The queued state is later consumed when controller reset completion drains pending_resets.
Draining each pending request propagates the controller-reset success or failure result.
After assigning the reset result, the loop removes and resumes each queued bdev I/O.
Resuming queued resets leads to unfreezing and completion of retained reset resources.
Completing and releasing both reset requests produces the success or failure values asserted by the test.
The observed pair of reset results is asserted by test_pending_reset in both normal and removal paths.

disconfirming_checks.statement: Removing the controller during reset must make both the active and pending reset I/Os fail rather than pass.
